# Model Catalogue — AI / agent integration

> Signed remote config for AI model routing and USD/THB token pricing. Merchant apps fetch a signed envelope from CDN, verify Ed25519 with a hardcoded public key, then resolve a model and price. GitHub and CDN are delivery, not authority.

This file is the contract for agents implementing a consumer. Human docs: [README.md](https://github.com/surapas3022/model-catalogue/blob/main/README.md). Reference client: [client.mjs](https://github.com/surapas3022/model-catalogue/blob/main/client.mjs). Schema (enforced by `build.mjs` before signing): [catalogue.schema.json](https://github.com/surapas3022/model-catalogue/blob/main/catalogue.schema.json).

Repo: https://github.com/surapas3022/model-catalogue

This hub is generic. It does not encode one product's feature names as build-time law. Consumers map their own purpose strings; unknown keys fall through to `purposes.default`.

## Do / do not

- DO fetch `config.stable.json` (production). Fetch `config.canary.json` only when that build was stamped canary at compile time.
- DO verify Ed25519 over the raw `payload` string (UTF-8 bytes), never a re-serialised object.
- DO hard-code the public key in the app. NEVER load it from CDN, GitHub, or this repo at runtime.
- DO keep a last-good catalogue, and a hardcoded floor (`version: 0`) so asking which model to use cannot take the product down.
- DO treat every rejection the same: keep using what you already have. The sample client's `startCatalogue` / `tryAdopt` never throw.
- DO bump consumer `CLIENT_VERSION` when you depend on new catalogue fields. Nested `model.price` requires `CLIENT_VERSION >= 4` (`minClientVersion` in the current file).
- DO NOT parse or trust `catalogue.src.json` from the network.
- DO NOT use `payload` until verify + adopt checks succeed.
- DO NOT pin jsDelivr `@latest`. Use `@main` or a commit SHA.
- DO NOT read prices from `model.input`. They live at `model.price.{input,cachedInput,output}`.

## URLs

Stable:

```
https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/surapas3022/model-catalogue@main/config.stable.json
```

Canary (signed only when someone publishes that channel on purpose):

```
https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/surapas3022/model-catalogue@main/config.canary.json
```

GitHub raw fallback:

```
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/surapas3022/model-catalogue/main/config.stable.json
```

Envelope: `{ "payload": "<string>", "sig": "<base64>" }`. `payload` is `JSON.stringify(catalogue)` with no extra whitespace.

## Public key (embed this)

```
-----BEGIN PUBLIC KEY-----
MCowBQYDK2VwAyEAdizLWdyfd6FznkuXBxX8fOG94aAF/ndNpwvMS07kj7I=
-----END PUBLIC KEY-----
```

Node.js 18+: `crypto.verify(null, Buffer.from(payload, "utf8"), createPublicKey(pem), Buffer.from(sig, "base64"))`.

## After the signature verifies

1. `JSON.parse(payload)`.
2. Reject if `version` is not an integer, or `version <=` the version you already hold. First run: compare against the floor's `0`.
3. Reject if `minClientVersion > CLIENT_VERSION`.
4. Reject if `channel` is present and does not match this build's channel.
5. Reject if `purposes.default` is missing or empty.

Copy `tryAdopt` / `startCatalogue` from `client.mjs`. `adopt()` still throws so you can log why; the boot path must catch.

## resolveModel(catalogue, purpose)

1. If `catalogue.purposes[purpose]` is a non-empty array, walk it left to right.
2. Else use `catalogue.purposes.default`.
3. Skip unknown model ids and models with `retiresOn` (YYYY-MM-DD) `<=` today UTC.
4. First remaining id wins.
5. If that list existed but every id was retired, try `default` once more.
6. If still nothing, use the hardcoded floor chain — do not invent a model id, and do not throw out of the hot path.

## calculateCost(catalogue, modelId, usage)

Prices are USD per 1 million tokens (`priceUnit` is `"1M_tokens"`).

```
usd = inputTokens/1e6 * price.input
    + cachedInputTokens/1e6 * price.cachedInput
    + outputTokens/1e6 * price.output
thb = usd * catalogue.usdToThb
```

Rates come from `catalogue.models[modelId].price`. Unknown `modelId` → `catalogue.fallbackPrice`.

## Purpose ids

Keys under `purposes` are opaque strings chosen by each consumer. This repo currently lists chat, OCR, embed, and similar ids as examples. After adopt, always read `catalogue.purposes`; do not hard-code this table as the source of truth.

## Catalogue object (inside payload)

Required: `version`, `channel` (`stable` | `canary`), `minClientVersion`, `publishedAt`, `usdToThb`, `priceUnit` (`"1M_tokens"`), `models`, `purposes`, `fallbackPrice`.

Each model: `{ price: { input, cachedInput, output }, vision, status, retiresOn }`. `status` is `ga` | `deprecated` | `preview`. `retiresOn` is `null` or `YYYY-MM-DD`.

## Errors

| what happened | consumer does |
|---|---|
| HTTP not OK | keep cache / floor |
| envelope not `{payload, sig}` | keep cache / floor |
| signature invalid | keep cache / floor; never parse payload |
| version not newer | keep cache (normal no-op) |
| minClientVersion too high | keep cache; plan an app release |
| channel mismatch | keep cache |
| every model in a chain retired | fall to `default`, then to the floor |

## Maintainer note

Bump `catalogue.src.json` `version` on every publish. CI signs **stable only**. Canary is `workflow_dispatch` or `node build.mjs --channel canary`. `build.mjs` validates `catalogue.schema.json` before signing; `node verify.mjs` proves those refusals. Private key never belongs in a merchant app.
